translate_en|mods/VehicleFire/42/media/l: Chance of debris after a large blast (percent)
One roll per large tank blast. At most one actually detached part at about 5 percent condition OR unusable metal is placed on a reachable loaded square nearby. Never creates loot from absent parts.
OFF: move cargo to the ground before removing its container in single player. ON: destroy it instead. MP non-empty containers always defer removal.
Seconds at normal speed for a continuously burning zone. Spreading adds delay; burning fuel can shorten the local time. The simulation follows accelerated game time.

A moving vehicle driven on tires burst by THIS mod receives gentle sideways drifting/oversteer, reminiscent of drunken driving. Each fire-damaged tire adds about 15%% of effect strength, up to 60%% with four. Standard deflated/repaired tires do not trigger it; no steering changes while parked.
Dangerous cargo increases tank explosion odds

When a trunk/cargo bed contains a NONEMPTY propane cylinder or petrol/diesel can, tank blast chance rises to 80%% with under half a tank (small pop) or 60%% with at least half a tank (large fireball). One roll per tank; empty containers or fuel cans filled with water do not count. Explosion Chance = 0 still disables blasts.
Fade paint on retained vanilla bodywork
Vanilla vehicles without an applicable burnt-model replacement gradually lose color saturation to zero. Original brightness and hue are kept. Does not replace textures or change modded vehicle paint.

Single-player only. Unlocks the Shift+I vehicle test panel: select a car, ignite, test two blasts, electrical shorts, runaway ignition, extinguish, or force complete burnout. Dangerous in a live save.
Adds tracking messages to console.txt. API failures are logged once even with this setting disabled. No destructive debug commands are exposed.

A charged, installed battery permits short episodes with at most two effects: lights, horn, alarm, door-ajar buzzer or failed cranking. Armed vehicles trigger an alarm on engine/cabin ignition. No power means no electrical effects. Wiring eventually burns out; episodes have a cooldown.
Disabling this stops new mod damage. It does not extinguish existing native grid fires or restore parts.
Critical engine smoke chance after a crash (percent)

If engine condition is below 20 percent, a heavy front impact has a 10 percent chance to start black smoke first. A later distinct hit damaging the front will ignite the engine. Repairing or replacing the engine cancels the pending fire.

Simulation seconds to consume fuel present when nonexplosive tank burning starts. Flare-ups increase local heat and can add up to two native spill fires. Extinguishing interrupts consumption and the explosion fuse.

One outcome is rolled per tank when it ignites. Normal odds scale with fuel. A NONEMPTY propane cylinder or gasoline can in trunk raises odds to 80%% for a small blast (tank below half) or 60%% for a large fireball (tank at least half). Set to zero to disable all explosions.

Default 1 percent per completed unsuccessful hotwire action. Not checked each frame, on cancellation, on a successful hotwire, or on an ordinary engine start. Ignites the cabin on the vehicle's floor.
Seconds at normal speed under direct fire. Faster game time accelerates this delay; nearby heat is weaker.
One roll per installed hood or trunk lid after 70 percent burnout. Passenger doors are excluded. Visible movement requires a model animation. The developer buttons bypass the random roll for testing.
Five quiet positional accents between 90 and 10 percent remaining integrity. Random 7-13 second spacing in real time. Stops after extinguishing; fast-forward does not speed up the sounds.

Two distinct fire tiles within one tile of the body cause preheating, taking twice as long as direct contact. Bumpers melt to 10 percent; tyres burst to zero pressure and at most 20 percent condition, staying installed until late burnout.
Chance of fire after a major collision damages a rear panel. The vehicle or nearby striker must have substantial collision speed and speed loss. More force increases the roll. Requires fuel.
A sudden loss of at least 2 rear-part condition points within 1.5 seconds, combined with a significant high-speed impact. Ordinary wear, repair and fire damage do not count.
Removes recognized separate tuning or protection parts at full burnout. Unrecognized metal parts are not indiscriminately deleted.
Native rust only. No black paint, soot skin or recoloring. Matching vanilla cars use their native burnt model after full burnout.

Percentage points of native sickness per simulation second, multiplied by smoke exposure. The default 2.0 gives accelerated, gradual symptoms. Existing sickness and poison are never cleared by this mod.

Adds native FOOD_SICKNESS while inside a burning vehicle. Above 90 percent sickness, continued exposure also adds POISON. No zombie infection is applied. Open, broken or removed windows reduce exposure.
Melt Immersive Snow on burning vehicles
When Immersive Snow is installed, fire gradually melts vehicle snow, ice and window frost. After extinguishing, normal weather accumulation resumes. No effect without Immersive Snow.
Heat transfer between adjacent vehicle zones. Higher values spread fire faster.

Single player: convert fully burned supported vanilla cars, including matched smashed variants, to the corresponding native burnt model. Preserves the same vehicle and full world transform. Conversion waits while occupied, moving or towing. Unknown mod vehicles and unmatched bodies are not replaced.
Rain and wind affect vehicle fires

Rain slows exposed flames without extinguishing enclosed fires. Wind favors spread towards downwind vehicle zones; occasional embers may ignite downwind vegetation or nearby vehicles, respecting native fire restrictions. Only burning cars are processed.
Creates bounded native grid fires for burning zones. Respects FireSpread and server fire restrictions. Off: damage-only from existing real flames.
Point and click the vehicle. Esc / right click cancels.
Irreversible full burnout, with part removal. Use a test save.
Enable the Burning Vehicles test console with Shift+I. Single-player only.
Bypasses the chance roll on modded vehicles only. The result and precise refusal reason are logged in console.txt.
Click directly on a nearby vehicle
Enter a single-player world and enable Developer Mode, then click here or press Shift+I.
